output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses is most likely caused by the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not by agency nurses. The "successful" hardware refresh skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules because of a file-format mismatch. These rules held back brief SpO2 dips, suppressed repeats, and sent technical alarms to the charge phone only. Since then, phones in Pods A-C get about twice as many notifications per shift, and acknowledgement time has doubled. Pod D was still on the old server and shows no change. Incident rates are about the same for core, agency and new-graduate nurses. Bedside alarm volume was flat, which argues against higher patient acuity and against the monitor update. Agency share is similar across pods. Don't approve the agency cap or the performance reviews: they would blame the wrong people. Instead, re-import and clinically validate the rules (about 4 hours of vendor work plus validation), then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Also review the apparent link to higher sick leave (plausible, not proven), and run a post-change test that covers all rules. I'm fairly confident, though dispatch logs don't show receipt at the handset.
